title: Motorcycle vs Car Theory Test: What's the Difference?
seoTitle: Motorcycle vs Car Theory Test: Key Differences (UK)
excerpt: Same format and pass marks, but different questions. Here's what changes for riders.
description: The UK motorcycle and car theory tests share the same format and pass marks, but the questions are different. Here's what riders need to know.
body:
The motorcycle and car theory tests use the same format and pass marks, but they're separate tests with different questions. If you want to ride a motorcycle, you need to pass the motorcycle theory test, even if you already passed the car one.

## What's the same

- 50 multiple-choice questions in 57 minutes, with a pass mark of 43
- A hazard perception part with 14 video clips and a pass mark of 44 out of 75
- You must pass both parts at the same sitting
- Your pass certificate is valid for 2 years

## What's different

- The questions are written for riders: things like riding in bad weather, protective clothing, and how bikes behave on the road
- The hazard perception clips are filmed from a motorcycle rider's point of view

## Where it fits in learning to ride

Compulsory Basic Training (CBT) doesn't need a theory test. You need a theory pass before you can book the practical motorcycle tests.

## How to prepare

- Practise questions by topic, especially the rider-specific ones
- Take full timed mock tests
- Practise hazard perception clips regularly
